about.blurb: Self-hosted voice, video and text for small groups. This server is somebody's, and these are the versions running on it.
about.mismatch: This tab is running older code than the server. Reload the page — until you do, things may behave oddly for reasons nothing else will explain.
addHost.description: Another relay installation. Its icon joins the rail; each host has its own login and password.
addHost.error.current: This is the current host — it is already open.
addHost.label: Label
addHost.title: Add a host
admin.bans.body: Everyone the installation stopped letting in. Bans on a single server are not here — those are lifted by whoever created that server.
admin.confirm.body: This one changes how the whole installation behaves, for everyone at once. The panel writes it down in the log either way.
admin.confirm.title: Change “{name}”?
admin.people.ban.body: They lose the whole installation at once: every server, every channel, direct messages and calls. The connection breaks off now, not at their next visit.
admin.people.ban.title: Ban {nick}?
admin.people.ban.warn: The ban sits on the identity: the key stays with them and stops being let in. A new identity takes a second to make — this ends what is happening now, it does not lock the door. Lift it on the “Bans” tab.
admin.people.device.self: This is the device the panel is open on — its key is the only way back in.
admin.people.empty: Nobody has a key here yet.
admin.reset: Return this tab to the defaults
admin.reset.body: Every setting on this tab goes back to what it was on a fresh installation. That is a dozen fields in one press, and it cannot be undone.
admin.reset.title: Return “{group}” to the defaults?
admin.title: Installation
admin.audit.body: Every change to the installation and everyone who made one. Newest first.
admin.audit.action.settings-reset: returned a group to the defaults
admin.upkeep.owner-link.title: Owner link
admin.upkeep.owner-link.body: Issues a fresh link that makes whoever opens it the owner. Any unused link issued earlier stops working.
admin.upkeep.owner-link.confirm: Whoever opens the new link becomes the owner, and you stop being one. Any unused link issued earlier stops working.
admin.upkeep.owner-link.warn: Copy it now — this is the only time it is shown. The server keeps a hash, not the link, and cannot show it again.
admin.upkeep.retention-run.title: Run the retention sweep
admin.upkeep.retention-run.body: Removes what is older than the retention policy, without waiting for the hourly timer.
admin.upkeep.retention-run.confirm: Messages older than the retention policy will be removed. This cannot be undone.
admin.upkeep.files-sweep.title: Sweep orphaned attachments
admin.upkeep.files-sweep.body: Deletes files on disk that no message points at any more.
admin.upkeep.files-sweep.confirm: Files no message points at will be deleted from disk. This cannot be undone.
admin.upkeep.revoke-sessions.title: Revoke every session
admin.upkeep.revoke-sessions.body: Signs everyone out on every device. Identities and their keys are untouched — people sign back in with them.
admin.upkeep.revoke-sessions.confirm: Everyone will be signed out on every device, you included. Keys are not affected — people sign back in with them.
admin.upkeep.export.title: Export settings
admin.upkeep.export.body: Saves every setting to a file. Secrets are not included — the server has only their hashes.
admin.upkeep.import.title: Import settings
admin.upkeep.import.body: Applies settings from a file made by the export above. Anything the catalogue refuses is named rather than skipped quietly.
admin.upkeep.import.confirm: The settings in the file will replace the current ones. Whatever the catalogue refuses stays as it is.
audio.unlock: Your browser muted the sound — tap to turn it on
call.delivery: Reaches them only if relay is open — the web app or the desktop/mobile app. Mobile web in the background won't catch it.

call.refusal.disabled: Calls are turned off on this installation
call.refusal.rate: Too many calls — try again in a bit
channel.mode.confirm.body.p2p: Voice in this channel goes back to direct connections between participants, with no media server in between.
channel.mode.confirm.body.sfu: Voice in this channel starts going through the media server: everyone sends their audio once instead of once per participant — that is what carries a call of four and up with video.

channel.mode.confirm.occupied.one: {count} person is on air right now — the break happens in front of them.
channel.mode.confirm.occupied.other: {count} people are on air right now — the break happens in front of them.

channel.mode.confirm.warning: The call breaks for a couple of seconds: everyone in the channel reconnects over the new transport.
channel.mode.locked: The media server is not running — direct calls only
channel.mode.p2p: Direct between participants. Click to route through the media server
channel.mode.sfu: Routed through the media server. Click to call directly
channels.mainFixed: The main server has a fixed set of channels — create your own server.
channels.noAnswer: The server did not answer — try again.
channels.refusal.badName: An empty name will not do for a channel.

channels.refusal.limitServer: This server already holds {count} channels — that is the ceiling. Delete one you no longer need.
channels.refusal.notOwner: Only the person who created this channel can change it.
channels.refusal.occupied: There are people in the channel — let them leave first.

channels.refusal.occupiedCount.one: {count} person is in the channel right now — let them leave first.
channels.refusal.occupiedCount.other: {count} people are in the channel right now — let them leave first.

chat.history.ephemeral: This installation keeps no history: messages are gone within the minute.
chat.history.edge: Messages older than {days} days are deleted.

chat.upload.tooBig: The file “{name}” is over {limit} — not added.

devices.admit.hint: The new device shows six digits and a code to scan. Only a device that is already signed in can let another one in.
devices.intro: Every device has a key of its own, and together they are you. This is where you see them — and close the ones you no longer hold.
devices.link: Link this device to an identity you already have
devices.link.hint: Only while this identity is still empty: linking joins a new device, it does not merge two histories.
devices.revoke.body: “{name}” is signed out at once, and its key is not let back in. To use it again you would have to link it anew.
dm.empty.body: There's no one here yet — open a new conversation with the + button above.
dm.empty.title: No conversations yet
dm.join.forbidden: This conversation isn't open to you anymore.
dm.privacy: Direct messages are addressed to one person, but they aren't hidden from the installation's owner.
dm.search.limited: Showing the first {limit} — narrow your search if you don't see who you're looking for.
dm.start: This is the beginning of your conversation with {peer}. Say hello.
dm.title: Direct
grid.alone: you are alone in the channel — invite the others
guest.ended.canReturn: The same link brings you back while the invitation lasts.
guest.ended.expired: The invitation has expired — ask for a new link to come back.
guest.ended.title: Call ended
guest.expired: The invitation has expired — ask for a new link.
guest.invite.body: Say who you are — and you are on air. Guest access works for this channel only.
guest.invite.body.listen: Say who you are — and you are on air as a listener. This channel is password-protected: you will hear everyone, but cannot speak.
guest.kicked.body: Someone in “{channel}” removed you from the call. The link will let you back in an hour.
guest.kicked.title: You were removed
guest.listen.note: No microphone needed — the browser will not ask for one.
guest.listen.title: This channel is password-protected: the link lets you listen, not speak
guest.mic.denied: No microphone access. Allow it in your browser and try again.
guest.mic.note: The browser will ask for microphone access — there is no going on air without it.
guest.reroll.name: Generate another name
hotkey.deafen.hint: Silence the whole channel (the microphone goes off too).
hotkey.muteMic.hint: Mute and unmute your own microphone.
identity.body: This device has just created your key, and the key never leaves it. That key is who you are here: no password, no sign-up — and nothing to recover if every device is lost.
identity.fail.crypto.body: relay knows people by a key the browser creates and keeps for them. This one cannot do that — or the page is not served over https. Open relay over https, or use a current Chrome, Firefox or Safari.
identity.fail.crypto.title: This browser cannot hold a key
identity.fail.engine.body: Your key is here, but signing with it failed. That is usually temporary.
identity.fail.engine.title: The key did not answer
identity.fail.gate.body: Access to this installation has to be confirmed with the site password again. Your key and your identity are untouched.
identity.fail.gate.title: The pass to this server expired
identity.fail.keychain.body: The desktop app keeps your key in the system keychain, and the system would not give it back. Let relay use the keychain — on Linux, make sure the app can write to its own config folder — and try again. Nothing is lost: the key is still where it was.
identity.fail.keychain.title: The system will not give up the key
identity.fail.network.body: Could not reach relay to prove who you are. Check the connection and try again.
identity.fail.network.title: The server did not answer
identity.fail.revoked.body: This device was revoked from your identity — most likely by you, from another one. Link it again from a device you still have.
identity.fail.revoked.title: This device was revoked
identity.fail.shell.body: The desktop app keeps its key itself, and this build cannot do it yet. Update the app, or use relay in a browser meanwhile.
identity.fail.shell.title: This app is too old for keys
identity.fail.storage.body: Private mode, or site data is blocked: the browser will not keep the key. A key that disappears with the tab would make you a new person on every visit, so relay would rather stop here. Open relay in a normal window, or allow it to store site data.
identity.fail.storage.title: The key has nowhere to live
identity.fingerprint.hint: The fingerprint of your key. It tells you apart from anyone with the same name.
identity.haveOne: Already have an identity? Link this device
identity.nick.failed: The name did not save. Try again.
identity.note: Names are not unique. It is the key that identifies you — the picture above is drawn from it.
identity.title: Pick a name
invite.dialog.description: A guest follows the link without a password — straight into this voice channel.
invite.dialog.failed: Could not create the invitation. Check your connection and try again.
invite.dialog.listen: This channel is password-protected, so the link only lets a guest listen — speaking still takes the password.
invite.dialog.note: The link lasts 24 hours and any number of guests can use it. Chats and other channels stay out of reach.
invite.dialog.title: Invite to “{channel}”
invite.invalid.body: The link has expired or was damaged. Ask whoever invited you for a new one — links last 24 hours.
invite.invalid.title: Invitation is no longer valid
invite.title: Call invitation
lightbox.hint: wheel — zoom · double click · drag — pan · Esc — close
lightbox.title: Image

media.error.constraints: the device does not support the requested settings
media.error.denied: permission denied. Allow the camera and microphone for this site (the 🔒 icon in the address bar), and on macOS also the browser itself in System Settings → Privacy
media.error.insecure: the browser blocked access: the page must be served over HTTPS
media.error.notFound: device not found. Check that the microphone is plugged in
media.error.timeout: the device did not answer. Try again

moderation.ban.body.everywhere: The key stops being let into this installation at all: the connection breaks off now, and it will not be accepted back.
moderation.ban.body.server: The key stops being let into «{server}»: the server disappears from their rack and the channels close. The rest of the installation stays open to them.
moderation.ban.fail.forbidden: This is not yours to moderate. Only the person who created the server moderates it — and the owner of the installation above them.
moderation.ban.fail.notFound: There is nobody to ban: the message is gone, or its author is a guest with no key of their own.
moderation.ban.warn: It is the key that is banned, not the person: a new identity is made in a second. This ends what is happening now, it does not lock the door.
moderation.banned.channel: You were banned on this server — its channels are closed to you now.
moderation.banned.body: Your key is no longer let into this installation. What was said stays in the channels; the connection is closed.
moderation.banned.title: You are banned here
moderation.bans.body: The only place a ban can be lifted. People are told apart by fingerprint — nicknames are not unique.
moderation.bans.title: Banned on «{server}»
net.title: Connection: {grade}
owner.body: This link binds the installation to the key of whoever opens it. Check that it is you, on the device you intend to keep.
owner.done.body: The key of this identity is now the owner's. The link is spent — a new one is issued on the server with `relay owner-link`.
owner.fail.badToken: This link is not valid. It was probably cut short when copied — take it from the terminal whole.
owner.fail.expired: The link has expired. They live 24 hours, and issuing a new one cancels the old. Run `relay owner-link` on the server.
owner.fail.network: The server did not answer. Try again.
owner.fail.noIdentity: You are nobody here yet. Reload the page — the key signs you in by itself — and open the link again.
owner.fail.used: This link has already been used. Ownership went to whoever opened it first; issue a new one with `relay owner-link`.
owner.title: Ownership of this installation
owner.warn: The previous owner, if there is one, loses the role. There is exactly one owner.
pair.admit.body: Type the six digits the new device is showing, or scan its code.
pair.admit.confirm.body: It becomes part of your identity: it will speak under your name and see everything you see.
pair.admit.confirm.warn: If you did not just start linking on a device of your own, refuse. An admitted key stays inside your identity until you revoke it.
pair.admit.scan.denied: No access to the camera. Type the six digits instead.
pair.admit.title: Admit a device
pair.fail.badCode: No such code. It may have expired: a code lives three minutes.
pair.fail.badSignature: Could not vouch for that device — the signature did not check out.
pair.fail.current: This is the device you are looking at. Revoke it from another one of yours.
pair.fail.hasHistory: This identity has already lived — it has messages of its own. Linking joins a device that is still empty; two histories cannot be made into one.
pair.fail.network: The server did not answer. Check the connection and try again.
pair.fail.self: That is the code this very device is showing. Type it on the device that is already signed in.
pair.fail.signer: Your key is here, but signing with it failed. Try again.
pair.fail.tooMany: Too many wrong codes. Wait a minute and try again.
pair.link.body: On a device already signed in as you, open Settings → Account → Admit a device, and scan this code or type the digits.
pair.link.done: Linked. This device is you now — reloading.
pair.link.gone: The code has expired. Codes live three minutes.
pair.link.title: Link this device
pair.link.waiting: Waiting for the other device to let this one in…
outdated.client.body: This tab is running code older than the server, and the server no longer lets it in. Reload the page; if it happens again, the app itself needs updating.
outdated.client.title: The app is out of date
outdated.server.body: This installation runs an older relay than the app you are knocking with. Nothing on your side fixes that — only whoever runs this server can update it.
outdated.server.title: This server is out of date
pins.empty.can: Nothing is pinned here yet. Pin a message from its menu and it stays at the top of this list — and in the channel.
pins.failed: The server did not answer. Try again.
pins.gone: That message is gone — someone deleted it.

pins.kept.other: Pinned messages stay. Everything else in this channel disappears after {count} days.

pins.limit.other: A channel holds {count} pinned messages. Unpin something to make room.

pins.mark.title: Pinned in this channel
pins.title: Pinned
rail.host.removeBody: Only your own list changes — the host itself and everything on it stay as they are. To bring it back you will need its address again.
refused.admin.bad-item: One of the lines is not an address with a mask.
refused.admin.forbidden: Only the owner of this installation can change that.
refused.admin.needs-confirm: This one is not reversible, so it needs confirming first.
refused.admin.not-an-option: The server does not accept that choice for this setting.
refused.admin.not-found: There is no such person, device or ban any more.
refused.admin.out-of-range: The number is outside the range this setting allows.
refused.admin.read-only: This one is set in the installation's environment — the panel only shows it.
refused.admin.secret-path: A secret is not written this way. Use the button that changes it.
refused.admin.timeout: The server said nothing back. The value is unchanged — try again.
refused.admin.too-long: The value is longer than this setting takes.
refused.admin.unknown-key: The server does not know this setting — it is probably older than this panel.
refused.admin.unsupported: The server does not know this action — it is probably older than this panel.
refused.admin.wrong-type: That is not the kind of value this setting takes.
refused.chat.banned-word: The message contains a word this installation does not accept.
refused.chat.delete-off: Deleting your own messages is turned off here.
refused.chat.edit-off: Editing sent messages is turned off here.
refused.chat.edit-window: The time for editing this message has run out.
refused.chat.links-off: Links in messages are turned off here.
refused.chat.rate: Too many messages at once. Give it a few seconds.
refused.chat.read-only: The channel is read-only right now — nothing you send will land.
refused.chat.spoiler-off: Spoilers are turned off here, so the file was not sent — send it without one.
refused.chat.too-new: Your key is brand new. You can read now and write in a little while.
refused.unknown: The server refused, and this version does not know why. Try updating the app.
refused.voice.guests-full: This channel takes no more guests by link.
refused.voice.not-in-call: This conversation is between two other people.
refused.voice.room-full: The channel is full — there is no free seat right now.
refused.voice.screen-share-off: Screen sharing is turned off in this installation.
refused.voice.video-off: The camera is turned off in this installation.
renameChannel.description: Everyone will see the new name. The channel address does not change — history and invitations stay where they are.
renameChannel.title: Rename the channel
search.empty: Nothing about “{query}”. Try a shorter word — the beginning of one is enough.
search.failed: The server did not answer. Try again.
search.gone: That message is gone — someone deleted it while you were reading.
search.hint: Type a word from the message. The beginning of a word works: “mess” finds “messages”.
search.title: Search history
server.delete.body: The server and every channel in it disappear for everyone, history included. This cannot be undone.
server.delete.title: Delete server “{name}”?
server.noAnswer: The server did not answer — try again.
server.refusal.exists: A server with this address already exists.
server.refusal.limitInstall: This installation is out of servers: {count} is its ceiling. Only whoever runs the server can raise it.
server.refusal.limitPerson: You already have {count} servers — that is as many as one person gets. Delete one you no longer need.
server.refusal.occupied: Someone is on air in this server — it cannot be deleted while the conversation is going.

server.refusal.occupiedCount.one: {count} person is on air in this server — it cannot be deleted while the conversation is going.
server.refusal.occupiedCount.other: {count} people are on air in this server — it cannot be deleted while the conversation is going.

server.refusal.gone: The server is gone — the list has already caught up.
server.refusal.notOwner: Only the person who created this server can delete it.
settings.autostart.failed: Could not change the autostart setting: {reason}
settings.autostart.hint: relay starts minimised to the tray — no window opens.
settings.hotkeys.globalWarning: This key is taken globally: while relay runs, it stops working in other programs. Add a modifier (Ctrl / Alt / Shift) if that gets in the way.
settings.hotkeys.intro: Everything is off by default. Bind keys to the actions you want — they work globally while you are in a voice channel, and are ignored while you type in chat.
settings.hotkeys.ptt.hint: Works even when the relay window is minimised. Requires push-to-talk mode.
settings.inputLevel.hint: The bar comes alive during a call — say something.
settings.key.access.blockedAddresses.hin: Addresses and networks turned away at the door: 1.2.3.4, 10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32. A bare IPv6 address is stored as its /64 block — a single address inside one changes on its own. This is not a defence against load: the request still reaches the server, and a firewall in front of it is the tool for that. And it is not a ban on a person: a VPN or mobile data gets around it in a minute. The owner is never turned away.
settings.key.access.guestsEnabled.hint: The door for guests. Off — a link stops letting anyone in, whoever came by one is turned away at the next connection, and identities are untouched.
settings.key.access.guestsEnabled.label: Guests by link
settings.key.access.identityCreation.hin: Closed means nobody gets a new key. Those who already have one keep coming in, and guest links keep working — a guest has no identity to create.
settings.key.access.loginRatePerMinute.h: Counted per address. Zero — not counted at all; any number here also stops an office where a dozen people share one address.
settings.key.access.maxDevicesPerIdentit: How many devices one key may be linked to. Zero — no limit; lowering the number does not unlink anything already paired.
settings.key.access.newIdentityQuietMinu: A fresh identity reads but does not write for this long. Zero — writes from the first second, the way it always did.
Quiet time for a new key (minutes)
settings.key.access.sessionTtlDays.hint: How long a browser stays let in before it proves the key again. Passes already issued live out their old term.
settings.key.access.sessionTtlDays.label: Pass lifetime (days)
Turns the door off without forgetting the password behind it. With no password set it changes nothing — the installation lets everyone in either way.
settings.key.access.sitePasswordSet.hint: One password at the front door. Changing it kills every pass and guest link already handed out, and the old password stops working the same second. While no password is set there is no door at all.
settings.key.access.unlockAttempts.hint: How many wrong passwords in a row the door takes before it starts holding a pause between tries.
settings.key.access.unlockAttempts.label: Password attempts
settings.key.access.unlockLockoutMinutes: How far the pause after failed passwords grows. It lengthens with every failure and stops here.
settings.key.appearance.defaultLocale.hi: Used when the browser asks for no language this installation knows. A language chosen by hand wins.
settings.key.appearance.defaultTheme.hin: Only for those who have not chosen for themselves. A personal choice is remembered in the browser and wins.
settings.key.appearance.installEmoji.hin: One emoji beside the name. Empty — nothing is drawn and the name stands on its own.
settings.key.appearance.installName.hint: Shown in the tab title and next to the emblem. It is a name, not an address — the address does not change with it.
settings.key.appearance.loginNotice.hint: Shown on the identity screen, not at the password door: the door stands before any pass, and settings do not reach it. The text is not translated — it hangs in the language it was written in.
settings.key.appearance.rulesText.hint: Opened from “About”. Empty — the section is not shown at all.
settings.key.appearance.rulesText.label: House rules
settings.key.appearance.showVersion.hint: Off — the installation's build number disappears from “About”; the tab's own number stays. The warning about versions drifting apart goes with it: naming a mismatch without the numbers is advice nobody can check.
settings.key.calls.busyWhenInVoice.hint: On — a ring to someone already talking is refused instead of interrupting them. Turn it off where a voice channel is a room people sit in rather than a conversation.
settings.key.calls.busyWhenInVoice.label: Someone in a voice channel is busy
settings.key.calls.enabled.hint: Off — the call button disappears and new calls are refused; a ring already on its way rings out. Voice channels keep working: joining a room is a different thing from calling a person.
settings.key.calls.enabled.label: Calls between people
settings.key.calls.maxRingsPerHour.hint: Counts the calls one person actually places; refused attempts are free, and answering an incoming call is never limited. Zero — not counted at all.
settings.key.calls.maxRingsPerHour.label: Calls placed per hour
settings.key.calls.missedMarkEnabled.hin: Off — a call to a closed tab leaves no trace anywhere, and the person never learns they were called.
settings.key.calls.ringTimeoutSeconds.hi: How long a ring waits before both sides are told nobody answered. Long enough to reach the device, short enough that “no answer” still means something.
settings.key.calls.videoAllowed.hint: Off — a call stays voice-only and the camera button is not offered in it. Video in voice channels is switched on separately.
settings.key.calls.videoAllowed.label: Video in calls
settings.key.calls.whoCanCall.hint: “Those with a conversation” allows a call only to someone a private conversation is already open with. Stricter than the rule for a first message on purpose: an unread message waits, a ring goes off out loud.
settings.key.calls.whoCanCall.label: Who may call whom
settings.key.direct.attachmentsAllowed.h: Off — only text travels there. In channels files are unaffected.
settings.key.direct.blockFromBanned.hint: Off — someone banned across the installation can still knock on a private conversation.
settings.key.direct.enabled.hint: Off — the section disappears and new messages are refused. The correspondence itself is not deleted and comes back with the switch.
settings.key.direct.enabled.label: Direct messages
settings.key.direct.firstMessagesPerHour: Counted only for first messages to a stranger; a conversation with someone who answered is not limited. Zero — not counted at all.
settings.key.direct.privacyNotice.hint: Stands in the header of every conversation. A promise that does not match how this installation actually works is worse than no promise at all.
settings.key.direct.privacyNotice.label: Note about privacy
settings.key.direct.retentionDays.hint: Counts only while a separate term is chosen above.
settings.key.direct.retentionDays.label: Keep direct messages for (days)
settings.key.direct.retentionMode.hint: “Same as channels” is what happens today: one sweep walks the whole history and does not care where a message lies. Any other choice gives correspondence its own term.
settings.key.direct.retentionMode.label: How long direct messages are kept
settings.key.direct.whoCanStart.hint: “Those met in a channel” allows a conversation only with someone already seen here. It limits the first message, not the answer to it.
settings.key.direct.whoCanStart.label: Who may write first
settings.key.files.allowedKinds.hint: The server sorts every upload into these three. A video arrives as “everything else”, so unticking that carries off documents along with it.
settings.key.files.allowedKinds.label: What may be attached
settings.key.files.blockExecutables.hint: Today an .exe travels alongside a .pdf. Turning this on refuses them by extension — it is not a virus check, and renaming the file gets around it.
settings.key.files.imagePreviews.hint: Whether a picture opens in the feed or arrives as a plain file with a name. Nothing reads this setting yet — previews are drawn either way.
settings.key.files.imagePreviews.label: Image previews
settings.key.files.installQuotaBytes.hin: Past this the oldest attachments are evicted to make room for new ones. Zero — no ceiling, and the disk fills until it is full.
settings.key.files.maxUploadBytes.hint: The field only tightens the limit. Past 25 MB nothing gets through anyway: the browser refuses first, and the upload route cuts the body off after it.
settings.key.files.maxUploadBytes.label: Largest file
settings.key.files.orphanSweepHours.hint: Orphans are files whose message is already deleted. The same sweep can be run right now from Maintenance.
settings.key.files.perIdentityDailyBytes: Zero — no quota. The count is kept in memory, so restarting the server forgives everyone what they have already used.
settings.key.files.spoilerAllowed.hint: Off — a file asked to be hidden is refused instead of being sent in the open. Without the spoiler mark the same file goes through.
settings.key.files.spoilerAllowed.label: Spoilers
settings.key.files.uploadsEnabled.hint: Off — nothing new is uploaded; files already sent stay where they are and open as before.
settings.key.files.uploadsEnabled.label: Attachments
settings.key.invites.enabled.hint: Off — new links are not issued, and the ones already handed out stop letting anyone in.
settings.key.invites.enabled.label: Invitation links
settings.key.invites.guestKickCooldownMi: How long the same link stops working for whoever was shown the door.
settings.key.invites.listenerByDefault.h: A guest comes in without a microphone and asks for it separately.
settings.key.invites.maxGuestsPerChannel: Zero — not counted at all, as it is today. A link is reusable, so a number here starts refusing the next guest who follows it.
settings.key.invites.ttlHours.hint: Counted from the moment a link is made. Links already out live out their old term.
settings.key.invites.ttlHours.label: Link lifetime (hours)
settings.key.invites.whoCanInvite.hint: A link opens one voice channel to a guest: no identity is created, and nothing else in the installation opens up.
settings.key.invites.whoCanInvite.label: Who may invite
settings.key.maintenance.bannerText.hint: A line at the top of everyone's screen — a warning about work ahead, or a word about what has just happened. Empty — there is no strip.
settings.key.maintenance.message.hint: The wording that explains the closure. Nothing shows it yet — the door refuses without a word, and what people actually read is the strip below.
settings.key.maintenance.message.label: What is said during maintenance
settings.key.maintenance.mode.hint: Everyone but the owner is turned away at the door. Those already connected stay until they reconnect: the mode locks the entrance, it does not clear the room. The owner keeps the panel.
settings.key.maintenance.mode.label: Maintenance mode
settings.key.messages.maxLength.hint: Nothing longer gets sent. The server and the client cut by the same number, so the counter in the message box does not lie.
settings.key.messages.maxLength.label: Longest message
settings.key.messages.pageSize.hint: How many messages arrive at once while history is scrolled. More means fewer requests and a heavier first paint.
settings.key.messages.pageSize.label: Messages per page
settings.key.messages.pinLimit.hint: Zero — nothing new can be pinned, and what is pinned stays pinned.
settings.key.messages.pinLimit.label: Pinned per channel
settings.key.messages.reactionsEnabled.h: Off — no new reactions go on; the ones already placed stay visible.
settings.key.messages.replyPreviewLength: How much of the original message is shown above a reply before it is cut off.
settings.key.messages.retentionDays.hint: Counts only while the mode above deletes by a term. Everything older leaves on the next sweep.
settings.key.messages.retentionMode.hint: The sweep runs on a schedule and deletes for good. History that this change carries off does not come back.
settings.key.messages.searchEnabled.hint: Off — the search field disappears and the server stops answering search requests.
settings.key.messages.systemMessages.hin: Lines about joining, renaming and pinning. Off by default because nothing writes them yet — turning it on adds nothing until something does.
settings.key.messages.typingIndicator.hi: Off — nobody sees that someone is typing, and nothing is reported about your own typing either.
settings.key.moderation.allowDelete.hint: Off — a person can no longer take their own message back. Moderators still can.
settings.key.moderation.allowEdit.hint: Off — the “edit” item disappears and the server refuses edits; what has already been edited stays edited.
settings.key.moderation.allowEdit.label: Editing messages
settings.key.moderation.banNotice.hint: Shown instead of the interface to whoever is banned across the installation. Empty — the standard wording.
settings.key.moderation.banNotice.label: What a banned person sees
settings.key.moderation.bannedWords.hint: A message containing one of these is refused — or flagged, depending on the setting below. The list stays on the server: handing it to browsers would hand it to exactly the people it was written against.
settings.key.moderation.bannedWordsActio: Refusing tells the sender why, and nothing lands in the channel. Flagging lets the message through and marks it for moderators.
settings.key.moderation.editWindowMinute: How long after sending a message can still be edited. Zero — no deadline at all.
settings.key.moderation.linksAllowed.hin: Off — a message with a link is refused, and the person is told why rather than left to guess.
settings.key.moderation.maxMentionsPerMe: How many people one message may call by name. Zero — a mention notifies nobody, though the text keeps the name.
settings.key.moderation.messageBurst.hin: How many messages in a row go through before the per-minute count starts holding them back. This is what lets someone answer three times in five seconds.
settings.key.moderation.messageRatePerMi: Counted per person. The ceiling equals the default on purpose: above it the server's own limiter refuses anyway, and a field that does not move up should not promise that it does.
settings.key.moderation.readOnlyMode.hin: Until this is off nobody writes anywhere: channels, direct messages and reactions all included. Reading and calls carry on as usual.
settings.key.moderation.serverOwnersCanB: Off — banning on their own server goes back to you alone. A ban across the whole installation was never theirs to give.
settings.key.notifications.desktopEnable: Pop up a system notification when the tab or app is minimised — today, only for an incoming call. Turning this off leaves the on-screen toast alone; it just stops the window that pops up over everything else.
settings.key.notifications.directSound.h: For messages in the direct section. Mentions in channels have their own switch above.
Only when someone calls you by name. Ordinary messages in a channel are silent either way.
The master switch over incoming signals. The click on a message you sent yourself is not under it — that is an answer to your own Enter, not news about somebody else.
settings.key.people.lastSeenVisible.hint: Off — the time disappears from the interface. The panel still knows it: this hides it from people, not from the server.
settings.key.people.lastSeenVisible.labe: Show when someone was last seen
settings.key.people.nickChangeCooldownMi: How long a person waits before changing their name again. Zero — as often as they like.
settings.key.people.nickMaxLength.hint: A longer name is refused. Past twenty characters the member list cuts it off anyway.
settings.key.people.nickMaxLength.label: Longest nickname
settings.key.people.nickMinLength.hint: A shorter name is refused. Names already taken are left as they are.
settings.key.people.nickMinLength.label: Shortest nickname
settings.key.people.pruneInactiveDays.hi: Zero — never, and that is how relay has always worked. The sweep removes identities together with their devices; it never touches the owner, the banned, or anyone who created a server.
settings.key.people.showFingerprints.hin: The four groups of characters under a nickname. They are the only way to tell two people with the same name apart.
settings.key.spaces.channelNameMaxLength: Server names go by the same number. Names already given are not shortened.
settings.key.spaces.creationAllowed.hint: Only new servers are affected: the ones that exist stay with the people who made them.
settings.key.spaces.defaultVoiceMode.hin: Direct connections carry three people; from the fourth with video the media server does. Channels that already exist keep their mode.
settings.key.spaces.lockedServersAllowed: Off — no new locked servers are created; the ones that exist keep asking for their password.
settings.key.spaces.maxChannelsPerServer: Voice and text channels are counted together.
settings.key.spaces.maxServersInstall.hi: The ceiling for the whole installation. Once it is reached, new servers stop being created for everyone at once.
settings.key.spaces.maxServersPerIdentit: Zero — nobody keeps a server of their own. Lowering the number does not take away servers already created.
settings.key.spaces.maxVoiceOccupants.hi: Zero — no limit, the way it is today. A number here refuses whoever comes next; it does not remove anyone already on air.
settings.key.voice.audioBitrateKbps.hint: The ceiling for one microphone. A call already going keeps what it negotiated — the number reaches the next one.
settings.key.voice.iceRestartSeconds.hin: How long a broken call keeps trying to gather itself back before it gives up and drops the person out of the channel.
settings.key.voice.noiseSuppressionDefau: The starting position of the switch for someone who has never touched it. A choice made by hand wins and is remembered in the browser.
settings.key.voice.pushToTalkDefault.hin: The starting position of the switch for someone who has never touched it. A choice made by hand wins and is remembered in the browser.
settings.key.voice.screenShareEnabled.hi: Off — a new share is refused and the person is told why.
settings.key.voice.sfuSecretSet.hint: Signs the pass to the media server. Its value never leaves the server either.
settings.key.voice.sfuSecretSet.label: Media server secret
settings.key.voice.sfuThreshold.hint: Counted without yourself. Below the threshold a fallen media server sends the call back to direct connections; at it and above, waiting for the server is the honest choice.
settings.key.voice.sfuThreshold.label: Hold on to the media server from (people)
settings.key.voice.sfuUrl.hint: Where calls of four and up go. Empty — there is no media server, and every call runs on direct connections.
settings.key.voice.sfuUrl.label: Media server address
settings.key.voice.turnSecretSet.hint: Signs the temporary credentials for TURN. Its value never leaves the server — the panel only says whether it is there at all.
settings.key.voice.turnSecretSet.label: TURN secret
settings.key.voice.turnUrls.hint: The relay that carries a call through an unfriendly network. It is read by more than the API: coturn next door starts from the same file, and a value edited here would drift away from the one actually listening.
settings.key.voice.turnUrls.label: TURN addresses
settings.key.voice.videoBitrateKbps.hint: The ceiling for one camera or one shared screen. Lower it where the channel is narrow: the picture gets coarser and the sound does not suffer.
settings.key.voice.videoEnabled.hint: Off — the camera cannot be turned on, and it is cleared out of what others are told: a tile promising a picture that never arrives is worse than no tile.
settings.key.voice.videoEnabled.label: Camera in calls
settings.language.hint: Interface language. Detected from your browser the first time.
settings.lightTheme.hint: Switch the interface between dark and light.
settings.noiseSuppression.hint: Removes background noise from your microphone.
settings.pushToTalk.hint: The microphone is open only while you hold the space bar.
settings.title: Settings
settings.updates.idle: relay checks for them on start.
settings.updates.upToDate: You are on the latest version
sidebar.empty: Nothing here yet. Create the first channel with the {plus} button next to a section.
support.insecure: open the site over HTTPS or update your browser
support.noWebrtc: the browser does not support WebRTC — update it or open relay in Chrome/Firefox
support.noWebrtc.gnome: the browser cannot do WebRTC. GNOME Web (WebKitGTK) has no calls at all — open relay in Chromium, Firefox or Chrome
support.webkitgtk.noWebrtc: calls are unavailable: the system WebKitGTK engine was built without WebRTC. That is the engine's limitation, not relay's. For now open relay in a browser (Chromium, Firefox, Chrome) — calls work there
tile.listen: Listener: hears the channel, cannot speak
tile.outro.peer: {name} stopped sharing — going back to the grid
toolbar.label: Toolbar
unlockServer.description: A closed server. Enter the password to get in.
uplink.bandwidth.title: Not enough outgoing bandwidth — your video quality is being cut. Turning video or screen sharing off, or lowering their resolution, helps.
uplink.cpu.title: The machine cannot keep up with encoding — your video quality is being cut. Closing heavy tabs and apps, or turning video off, helps.
user.nick.hint: Name — press Enter or click away to apply. It travels with your identity, not with this browser.
voice.toast.joinFailedMic: Could not go on air: microphone — {reason}.
voice.toast.micHint: Wrong microphone? The “▲” badge on the mic button switches it.
voice.toast.locked: This channel is locked: the server wants its password. Enter it again to get back on the air.
voice.toast.peerCannotHear: {names} cannot hear you: their call is direct, not through the media server.
voice.toast.peerUnreachable: Could not connect to “{name}”: the network is blocking it. Still trying — an admin should check the TURN server.
voice.toast.peersDirect: {names} cannot use the media server — calling directly.
voice.toast.screenUnsupported: Screen sharing is not available in this browser.
voice.toast.sfuDownDirect: The media server is unavailable — calling directly.
voice.toast.sfuDownWaiting: The media server is unavailable. Waiting for it: too many people here for direct calls.
voice.toast.youAreDirect: You are calling directly while the others go through the media server. They cannot hear you: rejoin the channel.
blocked.title: This address is closed
blocked.body: The owner of this installation has closed the address you are connecting from. If you share it with other people, they are affected too.
maintenance.title: Closed for maintenance
maintenance.body: The installation is unavailable for a while. Try again a bit later.
